reply.summary: Huang Xing's reply, addressed by courtesy names to Lin Hu, Li Genyuan, Cheng Zikai, Wen Qun, Yang Yongtai and Zhang Shizhao: he has their telegram, is glad the National Protection Army can enter Hunan and Jiangxi quickly, and asks when Zhang Shizhao will cross east to Japan.
reply.en:
To brothers Yin[qing] (Lin Hu), Yin[quan] (Li Genyuan), Song[sheng] (Cheng Zikai), Zhao[yun] (Wen Qun), Chang[qing]
(Yang Yongtai) and Xing[yan] (Zhang Shizhao): just as I was sending a letter, your telegram of the 20th arrived, and I
have respectfully noted everything. That the National Protection Army can enter Hunan and Jiangxi quickly is very good.
On what day does Xingyan cross east? I hope he sets out soon; wire me first. Xing. The 25th.

t1-0520.summary: The Military Affairs Council welcomes Huang Xing's arrival in Japan and asks for his guidance on domestic and foreign affairs, signed by Tang Jiyao, Cen Chunxuan, Liang Qichao and others; already printed in 1916 (護國軍紀事 no. 5). Transcription and corrections contributed by Harumi-Matsuba (issue #48).
t1-0520.en:
Mr Huang Keqiang: we have received your telegram of the 15th and learn that you have arrived in Japan, to our
exceeding joy. We, [Tang Jiyao] and the others, men of ordinary talent, have exerted ourselves to rise and punish the
traitor, and were just fearing that our rope was too short when you returned. We hope you will not cast us aside and
will deign to lend us your hand. You first called for the republic and are rich in plans; you have studied the
situation of the powers closely; in the future, domestic and foreign affairs will all depend on your guidance. The
whole situation hangs on it; we look to you alone to plan it. Tang Jiyao, Cen Chunxuan, Liang Qichao, Liu Xianshi,
Lu Rongting, Long Jiguang, Lü Gongwang, Cai E, Li Liejun, Chen Bingkun. The 20th.

t2-0520.summary: The six at Zhaoqing report that the Military Affairs Council holds only a name, its committees not yet organised; the Xiehe army will soon enter Jiangxi from Shaozhou; Lin Hu takes the Fourth Division; and Zhang Shizhao plans to come east to report in person. Transcription and corrections contributed by Harumi-Matsuba (issue #48).
t2-0520.en:
[We are] very glad that you have reached Japan. Runfu will tell you of the recent situation, so that the plan of action
can be settled. The Military Affairs Council holds only an empty name; the committee, the delegates' meeting and the
rest are not yet organised. The Xiehe Army can be assembled within ten days and will then enter Jiangxi from
Shao[zhou]. Unless we wait until Ganqing's Xiehe troops enter Hunan and [?Jiangxi], we fear we can hardly speak out.
Feng and Duan are mediating. Here the business of acting chief of staff is provisionally arranged, [Li Gen]yuan taking
it alone. [Lin] Hu is made commander of the Fourth Division, gathers his old units, about ten thousand, and will also
go out into Jiangxi at once. [Cheng Zi]kai is moving the Hunan troops in Guangdong to [?go out] into Hunan at once.
[Zhang Shi]zhao plans to come east to report the recent situation in person.

snip.cap: Huang Xing’s reply, 25 May 1916: the three-kana telegram as handed in

system: The standard Chinese telegraph code written as three kana per four-digit code by a fixed arithmetic rule (Tomokiyo's formula) and sent in romaji.
